problems.title: Absence of a rejection template does not establish semantic harmful compliance
problems.source_location: Appendix A.4.1, Eq. (12), arXiv v3 PDF pp. 16–17; Tables 5–6, p. 18; Section 4.4 and Table 4, p. 8.
claim: Paraphrase: Appendix A.4.1 states that an attack is successful when the response contains none of the predefined rejection templates; the ASR is the proportion of such responses. It describes these as non-rejecting and potentially unsafe responses, and states that automatic exact matching is used without manual labeling for this metric. See Eq. (12), pp. 16–17, and Tables 5–6, p. 18. The black-box figures of \(75.24\%\), \(70.06\%\), and \(56.55\%\) appear in Table 4 and Section 4.4 on p. 8.
The definition itself is explicit. The concern arises only when this operational score is interpreted as the proportion of responses that semantically assist a prohibited task.
analysis: For a prohibited request, the response ‘I decline.’ refuses assistance. The listed template ‘I must decline’ is not its substring, and the other listed templates do not match it. The lexical rule therefore labels success without semantic harmful compliance. This disproves equivalence between the two predicates; it does not recompute a reported success rate.
result: The latest paper retains lexical non-rejection as the operational ASR. It is not identical to substantive harmful compliance. The paper explicitly calls non-rejecting responses potentially unsafe and separately reports human semantic evaluation; no actual response-level error rate or revised ranking is established.
repair: Describe the score as a lexical non-rejection proxy and distinguish it from a separate semantic compliance assessment. No new attack or unsafe-response generation is involved.
problems.impact_rationale: The refusal witness limits interpretation of the primary proxy, while the explicitly disclosed definition and separate human assessment prevent a broader finding about attack effectiveness.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: The current metric still admits a harmless refusal as lexical success. This is a Minor interpretation limitation, with no recomputation of ASR or refutation of the attack mechanism.
